answer: One concrete defense is a bonded-identity registry: before an agent may transact, it escrows a stake sized to its claimed volume, and randomly drawn peers attest a sample of its work. A sybil operator spinning up a thousand keys must post a thousand independent stakes and survive identical sampling, so every fake identity costs real capital instead of a free signature. Slashed stakes pay the attestors, making forgery a losing trade. No ivory-tower theory is required: the atlas of participants is priced, and each ridge of the market carries a measurable entry fee.
